crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Download the position description School Crossing Supervisor PD 144.04 KB [PDF] 23 November 2022 How to apply Learn more about this rewarding role by reading the position description above. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Business and Policy Analyst (15275) Requisition ID 15275 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Do you love data like we do? A unique role focused on technology, innovation and with high exposure! $87,101 - $100,905 per annum plus Super and RDO leave 4:1 hybrid working offered This is a specialised role offering diverse responsibilities and exposure across the organisation, with close connection to senior leadership. The role provides an opportunity to build experience across technology, data analytics, project management, business improvement and corporate functions. A little bit about the role The Business and Policy Analyst will play a key role in supporting parking technology, innovation and continuous improvement, including analysing data, monitoring performance and providing insights to inform operational strategy and service improvements. A parking technology roadmap is being progressed, and this role will be a key contributor delivering it alongside the Business and Policy Lead and Manager Civic Services. The role also includes ongoing administrative responsibilities, including producing insightful reporting and metrics, supporting contract management and vendor meetings, procurement and invoice management, and maintaining strong business records. Exciting projects and business improvement opportunities will also be assigned as capacity permits. This provides variety and ensures the role continues to evolve and grow. Reporting to the Business and Policy Lead, key aspects of the role include: Leading innovation across parking technology, including market research, consultation and refining approaches with Parking Services leadership. Analysing large datasets and producing insights on parking operations to inform strategic approaches and future service models. Providing data and recommendations that inform strategic decisions and have a tangible impact on the regulatory services delivered to the community. Supporting leadership with parking contract management, enhancement and maintenance. Providing direct support to the Business and Policy Lead through the coordination and delivery of delegated priorities as they arise. Providing first-class customer service to internal and external stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner. Providing project management support for key departmental projects and continuous improvement initiatives. Managing invoicing, including raising purchase orders, receipting goods and maintaining accurate financial records for the Coordinator. Providing advocacy and quality assurance across Civic Services on key legislative and auditing functions. A little bit about you Your skills are the foundation of our success. The skills and experience you bring: A love of data, getting into the detail, and pulling out the insights to tell the real story of what’s occurring. Expertise in project management, continuous improvement and delivering outcomes to support front-line teams that are servicing the community. A fun and energetic approach to work that’s outgoing and engaging. Natural ability to manage personal time, to set priorities and plan and organise own work to efficiently complete tasks or achieve objectives within agreed time frames. Excellent records management and Microsoft Office skills experience, particularly in Excel and PowerPoint. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including demonstrated ability in writing accurate and comprehensive reports and correspondence. A sound knowledge or ability to gain the knowledge of relevant Regulations and Council policies. Relevant experience in a complex customer service/administrative environment both in person and over the phone, including proficiency in financial administration, preferably in local government or other statutory based environments. Want to know more? For further information about this opportunity please refer to the Position Description or contact Yvonne Hill , Business and Policy Lead during business hours on 9248 4444 for a confidential discussion. What sets us apart? A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. Staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships An investment in your ongoing professional development and career growth Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working With Children’s check. How to apply (follow carefully) Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by Tuesday 20 October 2026, 11:59pm . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. As part of our Technology Platforms team, you'll play a key role in ensuring our business applications effectively support Council services, business processes and strategic priorities. We are seeking a collaborative and customer-focused Functional Analyst to provide functional support, business analysis expertise and stakeholder engagement across a diverse range of enterprise applications. About the role Reporting to the Lead Analyst, you will act as the vital link between business users, service owners, vendors and technical teams. You'll develop a strong understanding of Council's business applications and processes, helping to resolve issues, support enhancements, gather requirements and improve system outcomes across the organisation. Key responsibilities include: Providing day-to-day functional support and troubleshooting for business applications. Gathering, analysing and documenting business and functional requirements. Conducting process mapping, impact assessments and gap analysis activities. Supporting system changes, testing and implementation activities. Developing and maintaining user guides, process documentation and other functional artefacts. Building strong relationships with stakeholders across Council and external vendors. Providing trusted advice on application functionality, enhancements and business process improvements. Contributing to system roadmaps, upgrades and continuous improvement initiatives. About you We're looking for someone who combines strong analytical thinking with excellent stakeholder engagement skills. You will bring: Experience in a Functional Analyst, Business Analyst, Application Support or similar role. Strong understanding of how business processes are enabled by technology. Experience troubleshooting application issues and coordinating resolutions. Proven capability in requirements gathering, documentation and business analysis. Experience with process mapping, testing and supporting system change. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. A strong customer focus and commitment to continuous improvement. The ability to quickly learn new systems and business processes. Desirable experience includes: Microsoft SharePoint, Power Apps and Power Automate. ERP and/or CRM platforms. Local government or public sector environments. Enterprise systems commonly used within local government. Why join us? At City of Boroondara, you'll be part of an organisation driven by innovation, integrity, collaboration and customer focus. You'll work with engaged stakeholders across a broad range of services, contribute to meaningful community outcomes and have opportunities to grow your skills in a supportive environment. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Branch Lead (15261) Requisition ID 15261 - Posted - Job Function (3) - Tenure Status (2) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Branch Lead Fantastic opportunity to take on a leadership role Permanent, Full-time position (35 hours per week) Kew Library $104,790 - $114,015 pe r annum (Band 6), plus Superannuation Are you an enthusiastic, customer-focused leader ready to make a real impact in a vibrant community setting? We’re looking for a passionate and dynamic Branch Lead to help shape the future of library services in a refreshed Kew Library due to reopen in early 2027. This is an exciting opportunity to lead a dedicated team, deliver contemporary library experiences, and contribute to a service that connects, inspires, and supports our community every day. A little bit about the role Our six libraries are thriving community spaces and in 2025/26 there were more than: 2 million loans 1 million visits 41,000 program attendees 91,000 enquiries As the Branch Lead at Kew Library, you will be part of an exciting period of renewal, helping bring refreshed library spaces to life ahead of the library's reopening. You will oversee the branch's daily operations, developing and leading a committed team and ensuring services continue to meet the changing needs and aspirations of the Boroondara community. This is a fast-paced and rewarding leadership role where you will: Deliver contemporary library services that support recreation, culture, education, and access to information Lead, support, and develop staff to foster a collaborative and high-performing team culture Build strong internal and external partnerships and community networks Contribute to strategic projects and continuous service improvements Champion community engagement and lifelong learning initiatives Support innovative digital and customer service experiences A little bit about you You’re an experienced people leader who is passionate about libraries, community-focused services and creating positive customer experiences. You will bring: Strong leadership and team management skills A collaborative and positive approach to staff development A commitment to innovation and continuous improvement Excellent relationship-building and community engagement skills Experience delivering high-quality customer services Library experience is highly desirable, but not essential Why join us? At Boroondara Library Service, you’ll be part of a service that makes a genuine difference in the community every day. You’ll work alongside passionate colleagues, contribute to meaningful programs and initiatives, and help create welcoming spaces where people can connect, learn, and grow. Employment Requirements Tertiary qualification in library and information science or relevant experience, is advantageous. National Police Record Check and valid Working with Children Clearance required. How to Apply If you’re ready to lead a busy, community-focused library and help shape exceptional customer experiences, we’d love to hear from you. To express interest in this opportunity please do so online via the ‘ Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 15 October 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. Please indicate which role/s you are applying for in your cover letter. For any further information please refer to position description , or contact Aileen Carter during business hours on (03) 9278 4020 for a confidential discussion. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. Council recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce for its employees and customers. To ensure equity of access to employment opportunities, Council encourages applications from underrepresented groups including people who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background, people from different ages, abilities, gender identities, sexual orientation and cultural backgrounds. If you require any additional support or adjustments regarding interview arrangements, please advise the contact listed above in advance. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Council is a child safe organisation and as such, some applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. A little bit about the role The Information Management and Archives Officer coordinates and manages Council’s archives, supporting the effective lifecycle management of physical and electronic records. This role is critical to ensuring that Council records are managed, stored and disposed of in accordance with statutory, organisational and operational requirements. The Information Management Archives Officer contributes to high-quality records and information management services through the classification, capture and distribution of incoming information; secure mail room and file delivery services; and support for Information Management projects, audits and continuous improvement initiatives. The role is expected to Maintaining confidentiality and provide responsive support to internal stakeholders is a key expectation for this position. Key responsibilities include: Coordinate and manage Council’s archival services, including the appraisal, classification, storage, retrieval and disposal of physical and electronic records. Ensure records are managed in accordance with legislative, statutory, organisational and operational requirements, including PROV standards. Maintain accurate and secure records management tools, registers and catalogues to support compliance and searchability. Respond to requests for archived records, including retrieval, distribution and return. The provision of timely information management advice, assistance and support to internal stakeholders. Identify and escalate complex, high-risk or non-routine records management matters. Liaise with external service providers, including archive storage providers. Support mail, courier and information processing services, including the capture, registration and distribution of incoming and outgoing information. Support information management projects, audits, digitisation, quality assurance and continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain confidentiality and contribute to accurate, efficient and customer-focused information management services. A little bit about you You will have a relevant qualification in records management or a related discipline, or significant demonstrated experience in records, archives or information management. You will understand the legislative and regulatory requirements for public records management, ideally within a local government environment. You will have relevant experience in the use of electronic document and records management systems, with a strong understanding of classification structure and information organisation. You will bring strong attention to detail, sound judgement, problem-solving ability and the capacity to manage priorities, plan your own work to meet deadlines with minimal supervision. A current Victorian Driver Licence is required. Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Description Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply If you are an organised and detail-focused professional with experience in records, archives or information management, and you enjoy supporting others to manage information accurately and securely, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button. All applications must be made via the online portal by Sunday 11 October 2026 at 11.59pm . No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Applications may be reviewed as they are received. Council recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce for its employees and customers. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Tree Crew Supervisor (15245) Requisition ID 15245 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Full time, permanent position with our Tree Team, located in Kew Lead a skilled team, build capability and teamwork and make a lasting impact through people leadership $89,002 - $102,806 plus super, allowances and overtime available 9 day fortnight including a tool of trade vehicle The Role We are seeking an experienced and motivated leader to join our Open Space and Trees team as Tree Crew Supervisor. You will lead a team of arborists and apprentices responsible for delivering Council’s 24/7 reactive tree maintenance services. This hands-on leadership role combines people management with operational oversight. You will develop team capability, support employee growth, drive performance and wellbeing, and create an environment where people are empowered to do their best work. Key Responsibilities You will lead, coach and develop a team of arborists and apprentices, building a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. You will support employee development through regular feedback, mentoring and performance conversations while promoting safety, wellbeing and exceptional customer service. You will oversee daily operations, coordinate resources and prioritise works to ensure service delivery objectives are achieved. You will also build strong relationships across Council, contractors and the community to support positive outcomes and service excellence. About You You have proven experience leading operational teams, building capability, managing performance and fostering positive workplace cultures. You are confident providing direction, building trust and empowering employees to achieve their best. With strong communication and stakeholder management skills, you can balance operational demands with a genuine commitment to people, safety and continuous improvement. You have strong communication and interpersonal skills, sound judgement and the ability to balance operational priorities with people-focused leadership. Your ability to motivate teams, foster collaboration and maintain positive stakeholder relationships will be critical to your success in this role. For more information about the role, please refer to the position description. Join the City of Boroondara At the City of Boroondara, we are proud to serve a vibrant, diverse and engaged community. Guided by our values and commitment to delivering exceptional customer experience, we work together to build a sustainable and inclusive city. Our people are passionate about what they do, united by a shared purpose and driven to continuously explore better ways of working. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Test Analyst (15243) Requisition ID 15243 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Great opportunity to be part of an exciting transformation program Camberwell location, full time limited tenure position until 31 August 2027 $104,790- $114,015 salary per annum (Plus super and RDO) Great opportunity to contribute to ensuring quality and testing for a high-profile transformation program that will shape how Council delivers services to the community. A little bit about the role Council’s Property, Planning and Permits (PPP) program is modernising how Council delivers services to the community. The PPP program is implementing Datascape and MyDatascape across property, planning, building and regulatory services, supported by significant business-process change, integrations, data migration and financial and regulatory controls. Council requires credible, independent evidence that the new capability is fit for purpose, operationally ready and sustainable through future SaaS releases. The Test Analyst provides hands-on functional testing across the PPP project’s customer, staff and operational processes. The role works with subject matter experts, business analysts, process owners, suppliers and users to translate requirements, process designs, business rules, user journeys and acceptance criteria into realistic scenarios, test cases, exploratory testing, walkthroughs and UAT support. The role works with employees at all levels across Council and with Senior Test Lead, will work with SaaS vendor functional specialists, migration and integration suppliers testing-tool vendors and specialist assurance providers. Key responsibilities include: Work with SMEs, business analysts and process owners to define realistic test scenarios, expected outcomes, test data and acceptance evidence. Apply risk-based testing priorities across customer, operational, financial, regulatory and service-delivery impacts. Prepare functional testing materials, including test scenarios, test cases, exploratory testing charters, walkthrough packs and evidence expectations. Coordinate testing inputs such as business data, environments, user roles, preconditions and SME participation. Support UAT activities, including business user support, defect triage, retesting and evidence review. Execute functional and end-to-end testing across process flows, user journeys, roles, regression, cutover rehearsal and production verification. Validate key business processes, including approvals, notifications, payments, refunds, hand-offs, exceptions, business rules and data outcomes. Capture test evidence and manage defects by raising clear defects, retesting fixes, assessing regression impacts and escalating unresolved risks. Support informed acceptance decisions by providing credible evidence on readiness, residual risks and functional quality. A little bit about you You will be a practical, detail-oriented Test Analyst who enjoys working closely with business users, SMEs, analysts, suppliers and technical teams to test complex systems, this role will suit you. You will bring demonstrated hands-on experience designing and executing functional, process-flow, user-journey and end-to-end testing across integrated SaaS, ERP or enterprise environments. You will be confident translating requirements, business processes and acceptance criteria into realistic test scenarios, clear expected results and credible evidence. You will apply a risk-based mindset to testing, focusing on customer, operational, financial, regulatory and service-delivery impacts. You are organised, analytical and collaborative, with strong communication skills and the ability to document test cases, defects, evidence and residual risks clearly for both technical and non-technical audiences. You will be confident supporting UAT, walkthroughs, defect triage and retesting, and have the ability to support business stakeholders make informed acceptance decisions. You will have strong knowledge of system, functional, end-to-end, regression testing, UAT support, testing, cutover rehearsal, and production-verification testing across customer, staff and operational processes. ISTQB Foundation or equivalent professional certification will be highly regarded. Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button. We are interested to hear about your experience as relevant to this position, there are some questions you will be asked to answer as part of your application for this position. All applications must be made via the online portal by Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11.59pm . No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Technical Test Analyst (15244) Requisition ID 15244 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Great opportunity to be part of an exciting transformation program Camberwell location, full time limited tenure position until 31 August 2027 $104,790- $114,015 salary per annum (Plus super and RDO) Great opportunity to contribute to ensuring quality and testing for a high-profile transformation program that will shape how Council delivers services to the community. A little bit about the role Council’s Property, Planning and Permits (PPP) program is modernising how Council delivers services to the community. The PPP program is implementing Datascape and MyDatascape across property, planning, building and regulatory services, supported by significant business-process change, integrations, data migration and financial and regulatory controls. Council requires credible, independent evidence that the new capability is fit for purpose, operationally ready and sustainable through future SaaS releases. The Technical Test Analyst provides hands-on technical testing across Datascape, MyDatascape, APIs, integrations, data migration and connected Council systems. The role implements and maintains the agreed test-automation framework and approved test tooling; develops reliable UI, API, integration, data-validation and migration-reconciliation automation; and performs manual technical testing where automation is not appropriate. The role works with employees at all levels across Council and with Senior Test Lead, will work with SaaS vendor functional specialists, migration and integration suppliers testing-tool vendors and specialist assurance providers. Key responsibilities include: Identify and prioritise technical quality risks by reviewing requirements, supplier specifications, APIs, interfaces, migration rules and acceptance criteria. Translate high-risk business processes into clear, testable technical scenarios in collaboration with functional testers, SMEs and technical teams. Define testability needs, including accessible APIs, stable UI selectors, logging, traceability, controlled test data, test accounts and repeatable environments. Establish, maintain and improve the approved automation framework, reusable components, tools, repositories, dashboards and evidence structures. Build and maintain reliable automated testing across UI, API, integration, data validation, migration reconciliation, smoke and regression coverage. Design and execute API, integration, migration, reconciliation, regression, cutover and production-safe verification testing across connected systems. Validate data flows, cross-system transactions, hand-offs, referential integrity, failure scenarios, retries, outages and recovery behaviour. Provide credible technical evidence, analyse defects, support UAT and end-to-end testing, retest fixes and escalate unresolved quality risks. A little bit about you You will be a hands-on technical test analyst with experience working on complex SaaS, ERP or enterprise system implementations. You will bring strong practical capability in API testing, integration validation, data migration, SQL or data interrogation, automation design and technical defect diagnosis. You are confident building and maintaining reliable automated tests using tools such as Playwright or equivalent, and understand how to manage testware through source control, reusable components, controlled configuration and secure test-data practices. You will have a risk-based approach to testing, balancing coverage, reliability, execution time and maintenance effort. You will be able to critically assess supplier evidence, identify technical quality risks and support robust regression, recovery, cutover and production-verification testing. You will have well developed analytical and communication skills and the ability to work constructively with functional testers, business SMEs, technical teams and suppliers. ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation level qualification and Advanced Level Test Automation Engineering certification would be desirable. Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button. We are interested to hear about your experience as relevant to this position, there are some questions you will be asked to answer as part of your application for this position. All applications must be made via the online portal by Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11.59pm . No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
